## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
One test needs fixing: `test_rejects_legacy_header` passes because its input has no `END` line, not because the header version is checked, so it does not protect the behavior it names. This review traced the stricter header check at `app/report.py:5` against all three tests by reading them, without running them. `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` does exercise the new branch: under the old `startswith("REPORT ")` check, the input `"REPORT v0\nvalue=ok\nEND"` returned `["value=ok"]`, and now it returns `None`.

## Changes
`parse_report` now accepts a report only when its first line is exactly `REPORT v1`. Before this change, any header starting with `REPORT ` was accepted. The pull request also adds two tests for rejected headers.

## Critical
(none)

## Important
- tests/test_report.py:10 — tests — Make the legacy-header test reach the version check — `test_rejects_legacy_header` builds `"REPORT v1\nversion=v0"`, and `parse_report` rejects that input at the `lines[-1] != "END"` check on `app/report.py:3`, before it reaches the header comparison on line 5. `rsplit("v1", 1)` replaces only the last `v1`, which is in the body line `version=v1`, so the header stays `REPORT v1`. That contradicts the comment on line 9, which says the test changes "the fixture's version to v0". Because the fixture also has no `END` line, the test passes with the old `startswith` check, the new check, or no header check at all. — This test cannot fail if the version check regresses, so it adds no regression protection, and its comment gives maintainers a false description of what it covers. — Fix: Use a complete report with a legacy header, for example `"REPORT v0\nversion=v0\nEND"`. Otherwise remove the test, since `test_rejects_unsupported_header_with_complete_report` already covers that input shape.
